title: Incompatible MSRV (Minimum Supported Rust Version) Bumps
damaged_code:
```toml
# Cargo.toml of a library (v1.2.1 minor release)
[package]
name = "my_library"
version = "1.2.1"
rust-version = "1.56.0" # Mutated from 1.40.0 in a patch release
```
pattern: Changing the Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) to a significantly newer toolchain in a minor or patch crate release.
why_bad: Downstream users pinned to older Rust compiler toolchains (due to corporate mandates or legacy OS constraints) will find their builds immediately break upon running `cargo update`, violating semver stability [42, 537].
detection: Any modifications to the `rust-version` field in `Cargo.toml` that require a newer compiler version than the previously tagged minor/patch release.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Valid if the crate explicitly specifies in its policy that MSRV updates are not considered breaking changes, though this still shifts churn onto users.
fix: Treat MSRV updates as breaking changes requiring a major version bump, or keep the MSRV stable across minor versions by avoiding new language features [42, 537].
source: Rust for Rustaceans, Chapter 8, "Minimum Supported Rust Version" [42, 537]
